objective: Admit bounded tool calls only when the tool definition, dependency graph, version, capability scope, argument data-flow labels, confirmation state, generation, and policy freshness match an approved contract.

research_inputs.finding: Formal MCP security controls require valid capabilities, argument containment, scope containment, expiry checks, tool-attestation verification, approved definition hashes, non-regressed versions, and known-good dependency hashes.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a deterministic tool-definition and dependency attestation receipt separate from existing schema validation and tool authorization.

research_inputs.finding: Production browser agents require programmatic action constraints, semantic/accessibility-aware controls, explicit confirmation for high-impact operations, fresh error feedback, and resistance to prompt injection rather than relying on model judgment alone.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL verifies argument sensitivity labels and explicit confirmation before admitting a tool call; the contract never invokes the tool.

features: argument sensitivity and destination data-flow labels
generation, expiry, replay, identity, and authority-boundary fences
decision receipt only; tool_invoked=false and execution_performed=false

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane admission overhead; excludes tool invocation, external servers, browser actions, network, storage, attestation hardware, and production approval latency

limitations: The contract verifies caller-supplied definition and dependency digests; it does not retrieve or independently attest a live tool server.
Argument sensitivity labels are caller-supplied and require a trusted upstream labeling process.
The contract emits admission evidence but does not invoke tools, inspect browser state, enforce OS sandboxing, or observe tool results.
The benchmark does not establish browser-agent success, MCP security completeness, production efficacy, AGI capability, or Linux superiority.

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the tool-attestation module, tests, benchmark, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain the KV-cache admission release tag
